units.text: 8. What is unique

Every single mechanism Symphony uses has prior art. What may be unique is the combination, and three of its parts. Each claim below names the observation that would refute it. Symphony's three claims, U1 to U3, were put to an adversarial search of 25 candidates on 2026-10-15 (research/taxonomy/verify/03); none had four of the five mechanisms below, but one, unsorry, has (c) and looser forms of (a), (b) and (d), so the claims are worded narrowly. Beethoven's three, U4 to U6, were not part of that search; they rest on narrower searches in research notes 04, 11 and 12.

The five mechanisms: (a) a claim made atomic by a git ref on the shared forge; (b) automatic release of an idle claim by a CI job, keeping the work; (c) a board and coordinator that run as CI jobs with state only in forge objects; (d) people's own sessions and agents in CI under one claim rule, on a flat-rate subscription; (e) validation of the shipped protocol code by exhaustive interleavings against an oracle written from the spec, with mutants.
Mechanism
Prior art

terraform-backend-git and actions-mutex (2020), DND-IT/action-lock (2026), Anthropic's C-compiler harness (2026-02), agentic-setup's create-only branch push, gh-aw's ledger and unsorry's claims branch

Leases (Gray and Cheriton, 1989); zulipbot, a hosted bot, unassigns an issue whose assignee does not answer within 3 days of a prompt sent after a week without an update; unsorry's two-hour reaper in Actions (2026-06); DND-IT/action-lock (2026-02) frees a CI lock held over 600 seconds by its commit's date, the clock Symphony reads, with no work to keep; agentsync flags claims idle for 24 hours as stale without freeing them
unsorry (2026-06) and gh-aw's work queue (2026-10)
aeon runs one agent in Actions on the subscription token, with no claims; claude-code-action itself
gh-aw checks TLA+ models of its queue, not its code; TLA+, P and Stateright are the established techniques
The claims
Claim
Grade
Refuted by
U1

Symphony is the only system found that puts people's own Claude Code sessions and agents running in GitHub Actions on a subscription token under one claim rule, with the claim, board, release and coordinator kept in GitHub objects and run by Actions
Inferred, from the search above
A system with four of (a) to (e), or with (a), (c) and (d) together
U2
It is the only system found that releases a claim by idleness since its branch's last commit and keeps the work under a renamed branch
Inferred
A system that releases by last activity and keeps the work. Caveat: the idle clock is the pusher's (spec risk 13)
U3

It is the only coordination protocol for agents found whose shipped code, not a model of it, is checked over every interleaving against an oracle written from the spec's text, with mutants that prove the checks bite
Inferred; the search was narrow (no paper databases)
A coordination layer for agents whose shipped code is model-checked
U4

Beethoven is the only system found that plans agents as Slurm jobs on the student's own subscription, reporting checklists as gates over each run's record, and contracts checked symbolically, together
Inferred; an absence claim from a search that ran out of budget; mostly unbuilt
Any system that gates REFORMS, CLAIM or a similar checklist in code
U5
Beethoven's launcher is the only tool found that starts Claude Code's Remote Control from an sbatch job through Open OnDemand, with nothing installed by an administrator
Inferred
A center-run Remote Control app for Open OnDemand
U6
beethoven-qa is the only project found in a narrow search of public repositories that makes contracts plus symbolic execution the required merge gate for code agents write
Inferred; a narrow search; the gate is a bounded search for most conditions, not a proof
Another required gate of this kind
What is not unique, and should not be claimed
An atomic claim on the forge: gh-aw, unsorry and agentic-setup have one.
Coordination that runs in Actions with no server: unsorry and gh-aw do it too.
Free coordination on a public repository: any of them gets free minutes there.
The subscription token in Actions: aeon and anyone using claude-code-action have it.
One issue, one branch, one pull request: Copilot's cloud agent works the same way.
The stack of Symphony and Beethoven: it is a design, not yet code (section 2).
